summary: Teaching the principles and algorithms of artificial intelligence and their applications to chemistry to second-year engineering students at the European School of Chemistry, Polymers and Materials of the University of Strasbourg.

highlights.label: Programming
highlights.value: Teaching Python for scientific computing and AI training.

paragraphs: Guest Lecturer contract at the ECPM engineering school (European School of Chemistry, Polymers and Materials) of the University of Strasbourg to create a course on artificial intelligence and its application to chemistry, including the fundamentals of statistics, the training of AI models, their application to chemistry and the teaching of the Python programming language for practical sessions.

My responsibility was to design the entire course curriculum, defining its objectives and organising the course into chapters. I then had to prepare all the course materials and exercises. I taught the course to several cohorts at the school (an average of 20 students per cohort), while also preparing the examinations and marking the students' work.

The course also included a group-work sequence in which students worked on projects designed to directly apply the skills acquired during the course. I prepared the project topics, ideally using my academic network to involve research laboratories in the projects. I then organised oral examinations to assess the students' work.
